thread.title: Amazon stock options suggest a big move after earnings

author: morningstar.com
title: Amazon stock options suggest a big move after earnings
text:
By Tomi Kilgore, MarketWatch
Options 'straddle' is priced for a 6% post-earnings move in Amazon's stock
The Wall Street bookmakers' line on how much Amazon.com Inc.'s stock will move after earnings suggests a tamer-than-usual reaction, but that doesn't mean it will be a snoozer.
That's because history shows that, of the biggest technology companies by market capitalization, Amazon (AMZN) has had the wildest one-day, post-earnings swings.
Amazon reports first-quarter results after Thursday's close, with the e-commerce giant beating profit expectations by wide margins the past two quarters. The stock, which rallied 2.7% in morning trade Thursday, has gained 7% in the three months leading up to the results, compared with the S&P 500 index's 7.4% drop.
Don't miss: Amazon earnings: 100 million members could be the company's Prime number (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amazon-earnings-100-million-members-could-be-the-companys-prime-number-2018-04-23).
Investors who bet on an options strategy known as a "straddle," which involves the simultaneous buying of bullish call options and bearish put options at current prices and expiring after Friday's close, will start making money if the stock moves 5.6% or more in either direction on Friday.
That's less than the average one-day post-earnings move of 7.4% over the past 20 quarters, with a median move of 8.0%. The average move for a post-earnings gain has been 7.6% (median 9.4%) and the average decline was 7.2% (median 7.6%).
Despite the "under" pricing by options traders, the stock is still expected to be more volatile than its large-cap brethren.
The average one-day post-earnings move for Apple Inc. (AAPL), the largest company by market cap at $838.0 billion, has been 4.2% the past 20 quarters. The average stock moves for both third-place Microsoft Corp. (MSFT), at $724.4 billion and fourth-place Google-parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), at $721.8 billion, was 4.6%.
Amazon stock gain Thursday has propelled it to second place at $727.2 billion.
The average move in shares of Facebook Inc. (FB), at $501.5 billion, had been 5.8%, before the social-media giant's first-quarter report (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-earnings-beat-estimates-amid-data-privacy-concerns-2018-04-25) released after the previous session's close sent the shares up 8.2% in intraday trade Thursday.
See also: Facebook appears to be bulletproof after stellar earnings report (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-appears-to-be-bulletproof-after-stellar-earnings-report-2018-04-25).
-Tomi Kilgore;
